title: International Music Day: how Yehudi Menuhin started it in 1975
dek: October 1 is International Music Day, started in 1975 by violinist Yehudi Menuhin through the International Music Council to bring people together.
keyPoints: International Music Day was first held on October 1, 1975.
Violinist Yehudi Menuhin started it through the International Music Council.
Its aim is to promote peace and friendship among nations through music.
body: Today is International Music Day, a quieter observance than most but one with a long history. It was first held on October 1, 1975, and it was started by Yehudi Menuhin, one of the best-known violinists of the 20th century, through the International Music Council.

Menuhin's idea was larger than a celebration of concerts. He hoped music could promote peace and friendship among nations and encourage people to share experiences and appreciate one another's ideas of beauty. The day is meant to recognize music in all its forms and from every culture, from orchestras to folk songs to whatever is playing in your kitchen tonight.

That last part is the easiest way to take part. Music is one of the few things families and friends of different ages can share without much effort. A grandparent's favorite song, a child's current obsession and a parent's college playlist can all fit into the same evening.

Many communities also have free or low-cost ways to hear live music, such as library concert series, school performances and community choirs. Local arts calendars and library websites usually list them.
Before bed, try asking someone in your home to play you one song that matters to them and to tell you why. It takes about four minutes and often leads to a good story.
